_timing: No narration yet. Each beat is the larger of the time it needs to finish animating and the time it takes to read, plus a 22-frame hold. This is a floor, not considered pacing — measure a real read and switch this topic to voiceCuts.

beats.lead: Every AI model has a hard limit on how much text it can hold at once.
beats.text: It's called the context window, and it isn't really a storage limit.
beats.note: It's a cost limit, baked into the maths of how the model reads.

beats.name: Attention Is All You Need
beats.role: Eight researchers at Google Brain and Google Research proposed dropping the older step-by-step reading of text entirely, letting every word compare itself directly against every other word in the sentence at once.

beats.lead: That direct comparison is what makes it powerful.
beats.text: It's also what makes it expensive. Double the text, and the comparisons don't double.
beats.note: They roughly quadruple, and computer scientists have proven this cost can't be dodged, not just observed that it happens.

beats.context: The fixed context window of every model size in 2020's founding GPT-3 paper: an entire model family sharing the same hard ceiling on how much it could read at once.

beats.lead: Every model since has been fighting the same quadratic bill.
beats.text: Pushing that ceiling higher takes real engineering, not just a bigger number typed into a config file.
beats.note: The comparisons don't get cheaper. Someone still has to pay for all of them.

beats.line: The cost of a model reading everything at once, all together.
